verdicts.rationale: params always carry v=2 so /flags returns the dict shape; the bool/str/else arms cannot fire. Thread 11 raises exactly this.

person_id is an unvalidated CharField; a malformed UUID reaches Person.objects.filter(uuid=...) and raises django ValidationError, which is not a ValueError, so it falls to the broad except and returns 500 instead of 400. 'Unhandled' overstates it but the actionable core holds.
The sibling reconstruction action maps VersionNotFound to 404 and VersionHistoryIncomplete to 422; the new action maps both to 400 (and uses 'error' instead of 'detail').
rollout_percentage == 0.0 compares against an exactly representable literal fed from JSON; an epsilon adds nothing. The claim is self-dismissed and carries no action.
distinct_ids[0] on an unordered list makes rollout/variant bucketing nondeterministic for person_id callers; thread 35 makes the same point.

The in-memory FeatureFlag copies only name/active/deleted/version/filters, so bucketing_identifier, evaluation_runtime and continuity fall back to model defaults in the override payload — thread 43's blocking finding.
this_condition_rollout_excluded is gated on is_zero_rollout in every branch, so exclusion by any rollout below 100 is never reported. Thread 25 is the same finding.
ConditionAnalysis.matched is set to all_properties_matched while the serializer help_text says 'whether this condition was the one that matched'. Threads 24 and 44 raise this; 24 is the earlier.

updated_at is DateTimeField(auto_now=True) (feature_flag.py:55), and Django forces editable=False for auto_now, so model_to_dict never emits it — the conversion branch is dead. Verified against django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:1368.
operator is emitted as format!("{:?}").to_lowercase(), producing 'noticontains'/'semvergt'/'isdateexact' instead of the serde snake_case wire names declared in property_models.rs:4-34.

Rust emits value: Value::Null for is_set/is_not_set filters (property.value is None per property_models.rs:75-76); the response JSONField has no allow_null, so is_valid(raise_exception=True) turns any such flag into a 500.
return_debug_info was deleted from the signature but posthog/api/person.py:1448 still passes return_debug_info=True, so that debug path raises TypeError.
try/except Exception: raise is a no-op left behind after the wrapping was removed; threads 23 and 38 both say so.

model_to_dict includes m2m fields and ManyToManyField.value_from_object returns model instances (django/db/models/fields/related.py:1952); analytics_dashboards (feature_flag.py:73) is not excluded, so any flag with a linked dashboard produces a non-JSON-serializable payload and the request 500s.
Three f-prefixed literals in the 400 body contain no placeholders — ruff F541.
The new timestamp tests mix datetime.now(UTC) with created_at plus offsets and retro-patch ActivityLog.created_at rather than freezing time; workable but fragile and hard to read.
person_existed_at_timestamp is imported inside the method while its two siblings from the same module are imported at feature_flag.py:88-91 — thread 5 exactly.

Only flags[key]['enabled'] is consumed; FlagDetails.failed and the response-level errorsWhileComputingFlags/quotaLimited are ignored, so a failed or quota-limited evaluation is reported to the caller as result=False.
The first error path calls capture_exception; the three new 500 paths only log, so those failures never reach Sentry — inconsistent within the same handler.
The claim's own refutation is right: AutoField keeps editable=True, so model_to_dict does emit id (verified against django/forms/models.py:108-115). Nothing actionable remains.
Self-ruled-out ReDoS speculation; regex patterns come from flag definitions, not from the request, and no action is proposed.
auth_token == *internal_token is a short-circuiting byte compare; thread 36's second point is the same, and it also names the subtle crate.

build_condition_analysis iterates only filters.groups; super_groups and holdout are never analyzed, so a flag gated by an early-access super condition or a holdout gets an analysis that cannot explain the result.

The only matching index is (team_id, scope, item_id); created_at is not covered, so the new ordered/limited scan sorts in Postgres. Pre-existing, and the claim says so, but the new query is what exercises it.

only_use_override_person_properties short-circuits prepare_evaluation_state_if_needed, so prepare_flag_evaluation_state — which loads cohorts, static cohort ids, group type mappings and group properties — is skipped entirely for historical evaluations, not just person properties.
A generic 'tests mirror internals' remark with no specific defect named; the concrete instances are covered by other claims.
No test references the test_evaluation action (grep over posthog/api/test/test_feature_flag.py finds only unrelated test_evaluation_contexts_* names) — thread 13 is the same complaint.
PropertyType is written as crate::properties::property_models::PropertyType four times while OperatorType is imported at types.rs:7.
A production action named test_evaluation reads as a test helper; naming only, no behavioral consequence.

match_property is called with the person-property map for every filter regardless of prop_type; cohort and group filters are keyed on ids/group props and produce meaningless analysis while type is still reported as cohort/group.
The comment says 'prioritize person_id over distinct_id' while the code prefers the caller-supplied distinct_id when it resolves to the person.
person_existed_at_timestamp gates a user-visible 400 and is untested; thread 13's required-coverage list names exactly the 'person exists but not at timestamp -> 400' case.
first_update_time, between_updates_time and second_update_time are all created_at plus fixed 10/15/20-minute offsets, so the ordering assertion can never fail.

find_version_at_timestamp validates tz-awareness while the two ClickHouse helpers validate nothing and call timestamp.astimezone(UTC), which silently reinterprets a naive value as local time. DRF hands over aware datetimes today, which limits the impact.

match_property returns Err for In/NotIn and FlagEvaluatesTo; unwrap_or(false) turns those into matched=false with a 'does not match' explanation, so cohort and flag-dependency filters are misreported as failing.
The action returns the full person_properties blob under feature_flag:read only — thread 12 raises the same scope concern.

The refutation is correct: the sibling endpoints use LocalEvaluationThrottle/RemoteConfigThrottle (BurstRateThrottle subclasses at feature_flag.py:410,432), not ClickHouseBurstRateThrottle. Nothing actionable.

The bearer goes to FEATURE_FLAGS_SERVICE_URL, defaulting to http://localhost:3001, over the internal-requests session; demanding TLS pinning for an in-cluster hop is not something a reviewer of this diff would act on.
Correctly ruled out — distinct_ids and timestamp are bound through sync_execute parameters, so there is nothing to report.
The slot really is shared (any non-phs_ bearer is treated as a personal API key) but the claim dismisses it and no failure mode on /flags is shown.

One global INTERNAL_REQUEST_TOKEN with no team binding, expiry or rotation now gates flag-definition overrides, property overrides, detailed analysis and the billing skip — worth raising while the surface is new.

get_person_properties has no error path (it ends in Ok(merged_properties)), so .ok() discards nothing; and if it were None, build_condition_analysis falls back to condition_matched, not to 'unmatched'. The asserted consequence does not hold.
Correctly ruled out; the queries are parameterized. No action.

With no versioned entry at or before the timestamp and timestamp < updated_at the function silently returns 1, so a flag whose activity log lacks early version changes reconstructs as version 1 instead of raising VersionHistoryIncomplete like the sibling path does.
Every touched test sets detailed_analysis/only_use_override to false and passes None for the override argument, so no test exercises the new behavior — thread 15 asks for exactly the missing case.
The comment claims .iterator() avoids loading all entries, then list(entries) materializes the whole (up to 10k) result set eleven lines later.

log_activity returns None without writing when activity=='updated' and changes is empty and force_save is false, so the version-less entry the test is named for is never created and the assertion passes vacuously.
The removed isinstance(timestamp, datetime) guard is asserted on by an existing test that expects ValueError('timestamp must be a datetime object'); that test now fails.
The parameterized case supplies timedelta(hours=1) for 'current_version' and then the body branches on _name and substitutes datetime.now(UTC), discarding the offset.
Self-ruled-out: the flag vector is owned per request (flags.rs:143), so the mutation cannot outlive it.

skip_writes is ORed from only_use_override_person_properties, which mod.rs forwards straight from the query string with no internal-token gate, so an unauthenticated caller can suppress experience-continuity writes.

A parse failure or a key that matches no flag only logs a warning and evaluation proceeds against the live definition, so a historical request silently returns current-definition results. Distinct code path from the Python-side fallback in thread 9.
The diff deletes a blank line before check_rollout with no other change in that function.
An explicit statement that the behavior could not be verified; it names no defect and gives a reviewer nothing to act on.
Considered and found correct — deserialize_optional_bool matches the existing config/version params. No action.

The slice does keep the newest 10k entries, which is right for most_recent_version, so 'corrupt the returned version' is not demonstrated; the real exposure is a dropped old delete leaving flag_was_deleted false.
Self-dismissed as bounded, and it is: per-property work over a flag's own condition groups. Nothing to act on.

logging.exception on the root logger with a redundant f-string interpolation of the exception, in a file that defines a module logger — thread 2 exactly.
Four info-level lines per override entry, two of which Debug-dump FlagFilters; thread 4 asks for the same downgrade.
